note: Ngoma lives mostly in village events and archive field recordings, so the playable set is small; Hugh Tracey's 1950 Tanganyika recordings are the classic way in.

size.basis: Mostly archive holdings: ILAM/SAMAP list hundreds of Hugh Tracey 1950s Tanganyika and Kenya dance-song items tagged drum or ngoma dance (the Sukuma listing alone runs to a dozen pages, Gogo four), plus a handful of commercial field-recording albums (SWP, Caprice, Acoustic Music, Honest Jon's, Real World). Commercial releases number only in the tens; the core reflects the few widely circulated albums and their standout drum tracks.
